note: A shortlist for Pastor Cole to review, not a list of approved church recommendations. Descriptions summarize public publisher or ministry information; reader and difficulty labels are editorial judgments. Source checks confirm book metadata and stated subject matter, not a full theological review. Naming an author does not approve every work. The public app books[] remains empty until specific titles are approved.

books.title: Mere Christianity
books.author: C. S. Lewis
books.description: Builds a reasoned case for Christian belief, then explores Christian character and what it means to live a transformed life.
books.reader: Adults exploring Christianity or strengthening their understanding of its central claims
books.context_note: Apologetics drawn from wartime radio talks; broad Christian common ground rather than a Baptist doctrinal handbook.

sources.title: C. S. Lewis official book description

books.title: The Screwtape Letters
books.author: C. S. Lewis
books.description: Fictional correspondence between two tempters exposes ordinary spiritual distractions, self-deception, and habits that quietly pull people away from God.
books.reader: Adults comfortable with irony and reflective discussion
books.context_note: Satirical fiction told through a devil's unreliable perspective; readers must recognize the deliberate reversal of good and evil.

books.title: The Great Divorce
books.author: C. S. Lewis
books.description: An imagined journey between hell and heaven explores the stubborn attachments, evasions, and choices that keep people from receiving grace.
books.reader: Adults interested in allegory and guided theological conversation
books.context_note: Fable and allegory about judgment and grace; present its imagined afterlife as fiction, not a literal account of heaven and hell.

books.title: The Knowledge of the Holy
books.author: A. W. Tozer
books.description: Reflects on God's character and majesty, connecting what Christians believe about him with reverence, prayer, worship, and daily life.
books.reader: Adults seeking thoughtful devotional reading about God's attributes
books.context_note: Devotional theology focused on God's attributes; a short book suited to slow reflection rather than hurried reading.

books.title: The Pursuit of God
books.author: A. W. Tozer
books.description: Calls readers to seek God wholeheartedly, surrender competing attachments, and cultivate humility, attentive prayer, and awareness of his presence.
books.reader: Adults seeking renewed devotion; useful for mentoring conversations
books.context_note: Devotional exhortation with contemplative language; review its treatment of hearing God's voice when planning church discussion.

sources.title: Moody Publishers book page and contents

books.title: Knowing God
books.author: J. I. Packer
books.description: Connects careful study of God's character with personal trust, worship, adoption in Christ, and confidence in his faithfulness through trials.
books.reader: Adults ready for sustained theological reading or a guided study group
books.context_note: Substantial devotional theology; current publisher edition is the 50th Anniversary Edition, distinct from its companion study guide and devotional journal.

sources.title: InterVarsity Press book page and contents

books.title: Evangelism and the Sovereignty of God
books.author: J. I. Packer
books.description: Explains how confidence in God's sovereignty supports evangelism, holding together human responsibility, faithful gospel witness, and dependence on God's work.
books.reader: Deacons, teachers, ministry leaders, and adults asking how sovereignty relates to sharing the gospel
books.context_note: Focused theological argument on divine sovereignty and human responsibility; a discussion candidate rather than a step-by-step outreach workbook.

sources.title: InterVarsity Press book page and contents

books.title: The Holiness of God
books.author: R. C. Sproul
books.description: Explores God's holiness and the human response to it, inviting deeper reverence, renewed worship, and a life shaped by his character.
books.reader: Adults beginning doctrinal study or seeking a deeper understanding of holiness
books.context_note: Theology for general readers using biblical encounters with God's holiness; choose the book, not the separate teaching series with the same title.

books.title: Essential Truths of the Christian Faith
books.author: R. C. Sproul
books.description: Introduces more than one hundred Christian doctrines through concise explanations and familiar illustrations, providing a reference for growing theological understanding.
books.reader: Adults and teachers wanting a topical doctrine reference
books.context_note: A topical theological reference rather than a continuous narrative; review individual doctrinal entries for fit with Bluff Creek's teaching.

books.title: Radical
books.subtitle: Taking Back Your Faith from the American Dream
books.author: David Platt
books.description: Challenges comfortable Christianity through Jesus’ call to costly discipleship, connecting everyday choices with generosity, mission, and obedience.
books.reader: Adults and older teens considering discipleship and mission
books.context_note: An exhortation to examine priorities, including a yearlong practical response; useful for a discussion group.

books.title: Follow Me
books.subtitle: A Call to Die. A Call to Live.
books.author: David Platt
books.description: Examines Jesus’ invitation to follow him, emphasizing transformed allegiance, obedience, evangelism, and the difference between cultural identity and discipleship.
books.reader: Adults exploring what Christian discipleship means
books.context_note: A direct challenge about conversion and discipleship; the publisher provides a discussion guide.

books.title: Desiring God
books.subtitle: Meditations of a Christian Hedonist
books.author: John Piper
books.description: Develops Piper’s argument that delight in God and glorifying God belong together, applying that conviction to the Christian life.
books.reader: Readers wanting sustained theological reflection
books.context_note: Introduces Piper’s particular framework of Christian Hedonism; a longer theological treatment than his shorter devotional works.

books.title: Don’t Waste Your Life
books.author: John Piper
books.description: Urges readers to place Christ’s glory above comfort and achievement, pursuing a purposeful life of sacrificial love and eternal significance.
books.reader: Older teens, young adults, and adults rethinking priorities
books.context_note: Written with the next generation especially in view; treats vocation, risk, and sacrifice through Piper’s joy-in-God emphasis.
books.edition: 2010 edition listed by the author’s ministry

books.title: Seeing and Savoring Jesus Christ
books.author: John Piper
books.description: Invites readers to contemplate the biblical portrait of Jesus, seeking deeper understanding of his character and greater delight in him.
books.reader: Newer readers and believers seeking Christ-focused reflection
books.context_note: A shorter introduction to Piper centered on the person of Christ, rather than a systematic theology.

books.title: The Spiritual Operator’s Manual
books.subtitle: The C.O.V.E.N.A.N.T. Method for Text-Driven, Christ-Exalting, Mission-Ready Preaching
books.author: Cole Permenter
books.description: Teaches a repeatable process for interpreting Scripture faithfully and shaping Christ-centered lessons, preaching, and everyday application.
books.reader: Bible teachers, small-group leaders, pastors, and serious Bible readers
books.context_note: A method guide for studying and teaching Scripture. The linked author page offers the digital edition; check formats there.
books.edition: Digital edition; author page checked September 7, 2026

books.title: Growing Up
books.subtitle: How to Be a Disciple Who Makes Disciples
books.author: Robby Gallaty
books.description: Offers a practical approach to spiritual growth through discipleship groups, helping believers develop habits and guide others toward maturity.
books.reader: New disciples, mentors, and small-group leaders
books.context_note: Uses Gallaty’s D-Group model; select the revised and updated edition when linking a purchase.

books.title: Rediscovering Discipleship
books.subtitle: Making Jesus’ Final Words Our First Work
books.author: Robby Gallaty
books.description: Combines historical examples with practical guidance for overcoming obstacles to disciple making and building relationships that help others grow.
books.reader: Deacons, teachers, ministry leaders, and prospective mentors
books.context_note: Offers ministry history and a step-by-step model for multiplying disciples; useful for leader preparation.

books.title: Love Your Church
books.subtitle: 8 Great Things About Being a Church Member
books.author: Tony Merida
books.description: Explores belonging, hospitality, service, care, and mission as practical ways ordinary members can participate in the life of their church.
books.reader: New members, church members, and small groups
books.context_note: Includes a discussion guide and publisher-provided group resources. Ray Ortlund wrote the foreword; he is not a coauthor.

books.title: Ordinary
books.subtitle: How to Turn the World Upside Down
books.author: Tony Merida
books.description: Connects everyday Christian faithfulness with hospitality, care for vulnerable neighbors, humble service, and sharing the gospel in ordinary relationships.
books.reader: Church members and ministry volunteers
books.context_note: Select the trade book with this subtitle. Lifeway also sells a distinct Ordinary Bible Study Book with different content and ISBN.
books.edition: 2015 eBook listing; trade book, not the separate Bible study workbook

books.title: How to Read the Bible for All Its Worth
books.author: Gordon D. Fee and Douglas Stuart
books.description: Introduces interpretation through biblical genres, helping readers consider original context before applying passages to Christian life today.
books.reader: Growing Bible readers, teachers, and study leaders
books.context_note: A guide to reading genres and interpreting Scripture, not a devotional. The fourth-edition publisher listing has no separate subtitle.

books.title: How to Read the Bible Book by Book
books.subtitle: A Guided Tour
books.author: Gordon D. Fee and Douglas Stuart
books.description: Provides background, structure, and reading guidance for each biblical book, helping readers follow its message within Scripture’s larger story.
books.reader: Bible readers wanting context and Sunday school teachers
books.context_note: A reading companion covering all 66 books, including Habakkuk. It supplies book context rather than a full verse-by-verse commentary. Audiobook narrator Trevor Thompson is not a print-book coauthor.
